_readme: local field key -> Zoho People field API name on the Confirmation_Process_Form (displayed in Zoho as "Candidate Information") — this is the org's actual candidate-intake form; the generic-sounding "Candidate" form named in ZOHO_CANDIDATE_FORM does not exist in this org. Every API name below was read live from GET forms/Confirmation_Process_Form/components on 2026-09-07 (see integrations/zoho/README.md step 2 to re-verify after any Zoho-side form change). Leave a value as "" to skip that field.
_education_flat_readme: Zoho's tabular sections cannot be written (see _subforms_write_status). These flat keys carry the same education data to ORDINARY Zoho fields, which do write. Fill each one in with the API name of a plain field on Confirmation_Process_Form once it has been created in Zoho's form builder; anything left "" is skipped like any other unmapped key. ug_* and pg_* are the first and second rows of the UG/PG table; edu12_*/edu10_* are the 12th and 10th rows; emp1_*/emp2_* are the first two employment rows, most recent first. A third row in any section has no flat slot and rides only in _subforms.

_unconfirmed_or_unavailable.hr_candidate_id: Zoho's Candidate_ID is a Number field; local hr_candidate_id is free text HR types in (e.g. "NANA") and is not reliably numeric, so it is left unmapped rather than risk an insert failing on a non-numeric value. Map it only if hr_candidate_id is made strictly numeric.
_unconfirmed_or_unavailable.aadhaar_number, bank_account_number, ban: No matching flat field exists on Confirmation_Process_Form. Education comes through the Bachelor/Diploma/10th tabular sections instead (see _subforms below) — export_zoho_payload.py does not emit those yet.

_date_fields_readme: Zoho Date fields expect dd-MMM-yyyy (e.g. 07-Sep-2026); the local DB stores dates as free strings from an <input type=date>, i.e. yyyy-mm-dd. Listed local keys are reformatted by build_payload() before being sent — see export_zoho_payload.py.
_email_fields_readme: local keys mapped to Zoho Email-type fields. Zoho rejects the ENTIRE record (error 7053) if any of these carries a non-email value, so build_payload() drops a value here that doesn't look like an email (e.g. an HR "NANA" placeholder) instead of sending it and losing the whole push.
_value_map_readme: local value -> exact Zoho picklist option text, for fields whose local option wording doesn't already match what's configured in Zoho. Applied by build_payload() before the value is sent. A field with no entry here is passed through unchanged. "_default" (if present) catches any local value not explicitly listed, e.g. a local option Zoho has no equivalent for.

_derived.full_name: sent as-is to First_name — the real Zoho form has a single Name field, not separate First/Last Name (an earlier version of this map incorrectly assumed a split first/last schema).

files._readme: local Document.field_key -> Zoho field API name of a file/Image field on Confirmation_Process_Form. Used by zoho_client.py --with-files and by app/services/zoho_push.py. Files are NOT attached to insertRecord/updateRecord as multipart parts — Zoho silently ignores those and answers status 0 with the field left empty. Each file is POSTed to forms/<form>/uploadFile with fieldName=<API name> first, and the encryptedfilepath it returns is sent as that field's value in inputData (see upload_files() in zoho_client.py). Image_1 (Candidate Profile Picture) is MANDATORY on the Zoho side — an insert will fail without it.
files._only_two_file_fields: Confirmation_Process_Form has exactly TWO file-bearing fields, both comptype Image: Image_1 and Signature (read live from forms/components on 2026-09-18). Every other key below stays "" because the form has nowhere to put it — marksheet_10/marksheet_12_diploma were briefly mapped to th_Certificate/th_Certificate1, which do not exist on the form (uploadFile rejects them with error 7013). Add a file field in Zoho's form builder before mapping any of these.

_mandatory_no_local_source._readme: Fields Zoho reports as mandatory on Confirmation_Process_Form with no corresponding local data at all. An insertRecord may fail on any of these with error 7052 until they're either answered for real or made optional in Zoho's form builder. Left deliberately unmapped rather than filled with placeholder text.

_subforms_readme: Zoho's Confirmation_Process_Form has tabular (subform) sections in addition to the main fields above. The column API names below are CORRECT — verified on 2026-09-18 against a populated record read back with getRecordByID, whose rows carry exactly these keys. What is NOT solved is how to WRITE them; see _subforms_write_status. Reads come back under a top-level "tabularSections" object keyed by the section DISPLAY name, which is what _zoho_section_display records; _zoho_section is the link name from forms/components.

_subforms_write_status._readme: Findings from a probe matrix run on 2026-09-18 against Confirmation_Process_Form. Nothing here is implemented — export_zoho_payload.build_subforms() still emits the old link-name shape and app/services/zoho_push.py still refuses to send it. Recorded so the next attempt does not start from zero.
_subforms_write_status.param: tabularData is the ONLY request parameter Zoho recognises. tabularSections, tabularinputData, inputTabularData and subformData are silently ignored — each produced a mandatory-field error list identical to sending no tabular data at all.
_subforms_write_status.section_key: Must be the NUMERIC sectionId from forms/<form>/components -> tabularSections[].sectionId. A bogus key gives 7027 'Invalid section id'; the link name (Bachelor_Education_Details) and the display name both fail with a generic 7200. So keying by _zoho_section, as build_subforms() does today, is wrong.
_subforms_write_status.updateRecord: Parses tabularData but rejects every row shape tried (12 variants: row-major, column-major, row-index keyed, field-id keyed, {value:} wrapped, stringified JSON). A section value that is an array gives 7204; an object gives 7016 'Invalid value [] for the field B_Qualification' — invariant across all inner shapes, which suggests Zoho never reads the inner content.
_subforms_write_status.insertRecord: Accepts tabularData with ANY shape, replies status 0, and writes nothing — the same silent drop that hid the file-upload bug. Five throwaway drafts confirmed this: every one came back with an empty row and no tabular.ROWID.
_subforms_write_status.api_v2: A second endpoint exists — POST /api/v2/forms/<form>/records (also under /people/api/v2/...). It is the only v2 route that answers; /api/v2/forms, /…/components, /…/fields and /api/v2/modules all 404. It demands an inputData form parameter (7019 without one) and then rejects EVERY value with 7023 'JSON parsing error'. That error is a catch-all, not a real parse complaint: valid '{}' and the bare string 'hello' produce the identical response, so no input shape can satisfy it. A JSON array value instead returns 403 'Invalid URL' from an outer layer. Treat this route as unusable until Zoho explains it.
_subforms_write_status.conclusion: Tabular sections could not be written through any available endpoint: v1 insertRecord ignores tabularData, v1 updateRecord rejects every row shape, and the v2 records route rejects every input. About 45 request variants were tried in total. Raise it with Zoho support before trying again; the files fix (uploadFile + encryptedfilepath) does NOT generalise here — there is no equivalent tabular endpoint on this form.
